solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Welsh runner on return put away stuff

parts.note: the Taff is a river running through Cardiff in Wales

indicators.note: on return asks for the word for put away to be read backwards

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A Welsh athlete, back home, clears away some belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but in crosswords a runner is often a river; here it is the Taff in Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff here means cloth or fabric, and taffeta is a crisp silk or rayon fabric.

clue.text: Bank job making an impact

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the work of a bank teller, counting out money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank job' hints at a robbery; it is simply the job of a teller, who tells (counts) money.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller's work is counting cash, an old sense of tell; and a telling blow or argument is one that strikes home.

clue.text: Writer's source? A stylish prison

parts.note: a fount is a spring or source
in means fashionable, stylish
a pen is an enclosure, slang for prison (as in the state pen)

explanation.surface: Asking where an author gets ideas, then describing a fashionable jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountain pen is a writing instrument, so it is a writer in the sense of a thing that writes.

clue.text: One leaving country before fighter's let in

indicators.note: let in means the fighter is admitted inside the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: An emigrant departs just before a soldier is admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has emigrated, often for political reasons, so someone leaving their homeland.

clue.text: Versatile player's ball game without wings

indicators.note: wings are the outer ends, so the first and last letters are lost

parts.note: ball rounders: rounders is a British bat-and-ball game like baseball

explanation.surface: A flexible sportsman's game is played without wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British school game similar to baseball. Taking the outer letters off BALL ROUNDERS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder is a sportsperson, especially a cricketer, good at both batting and bowling.

clue.text: Clubs twice invested in shabby old kit for assembly

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as money is put into a venture

parts.note: mean can mean shabby, poor in appearance
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
twice says the clubs abbreviation is given a second time

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are packed twice into a worn-out old set to be put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a construction toy of metal strips, nuts and bolts, a kit you assemble into models.

clue.text: A person of habit, male running kilometres

parts.note: on means operating, running, as a machine is on
K is short for kilometres

explanation.surface: A creature of routine, a man jogging some kilometres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person of habit' reads as someone with routines; the habit is a religious robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk wears a habit, the long robe of a religious order, so he is literally a person of habit.

clue.text: Peeved group of lawyers that joins supporters on pitch

parts.note: cross means annoyed, peeved
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Annoyed lawyers join fans at a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The supporters are not fans but the goalposts, which the bar links at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: On a football or rugby pitch the crossbar is the horizontal beam joining the two upright posts.

clue.text: Target section of north-south artery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a goal or objective
second meaning: the A1(M), the motorway stretch of the A1, Britain's main north-south road, read with 1 as I

explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the Great North Road from London to Edinburgh; its motorway stretches are labelled A1(M), which reads as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a goal or objective, the thing one targets; the road label supplies the second, visual sense.

clue.text: Tidy Berliner article found in airport

indicators.note: found in says the article sits inside the airport's name

parts.note: Orly is a Paris airport
der is the German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A neat man from Berlin writes a piece set in an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means neat and well arranged, the same as tidy.

clue.text: Place I quit to make money abroad

indicators.note: quit means the I leaves the word for place

parts.note: lieu means place, as in in lieu of

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their job to earn cash overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The leu is the currency of Romania and Moldova, a foreign money unit.

clue.text: Ignorant Oscar is abandoning state for sea

indicators.note: abandoning means the letters for Oscar and is leave the state's name

parts.note: Illinois is a US state
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winner is leaving America for a seaside life, knowing little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoning' takes O and IS from ILLINOIS, leaving ILLIN; FOR is taken as written, then MED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-informed means lacking knowledge of the facts, which is what ignorant means.

clue.text: Mediocre temp initially standing in for female domestic

indicators.note: standing in for means one letter replaces another, as a temp replaces a worker

parts.note: inferior means second-rate, mediocre

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of temp

explanation.surface: A poor temporary worker replaces a housemaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like a servant, but here it is the adjective for home affairs, as in a Ministry of the Interior.
explanation.definitionFit: Interior can mean internal to a country, as in interior affairs, which is the domestic sense opposed to foreign.

clue.text: Addict tours centrepiece of church, one attracting lots of interest

indicators.note: tours means goes around, so the addict's word encloses the middle letters

parts.note: a user is a drug addict

indicators.note: centrepiece of takes the middle letters of church

explanation.surface: A drug user wanders round the heart of a church, drawing attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of interest' reads as fascination; it is money interest on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at excessive rates, so his loans attract heavy interest charges.

clue.text: Does trainer broadcast a topic in metaphysics?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, as seed is thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a coach talks philosophy on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A raison d'être is a reason for existing, the kind of question of being that metaphysics studies; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: "Very old Tom" superseding name in horse's stall?

indicators.note: superseding means taking the place of the letter for name

parts.note: equine means of a horse
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An elderly tomcat displaces a nameplate in a horse's stable stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' looks like a stable compartment; it is the verb meaning to play for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To equivocate is to speak evasively to avoid committing oneself, a way of stalling.

clue.text: Purchase beef after reduction

indicators.note: after reduction means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a beef is a complaint, a gripe

explanation.surface: Buy some meat once the price has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' is not buying but a firm hold, and 'beef' is a complaint, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold or leverage, as in getting purchase on a rock face, which is a grip.

clue.text: Books in popular eastern landing place showing discrepancy

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: in places the books inside the landing place

parts.note: a quay is a wharf where boats land
lit, literature, stands for books

explanation.surface: Books at a fashionable eastern dock reveal a mismatch.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequality is a lack of equality or balance, a difference or disparity between things.

clue.text: Original claim a March girl's put in for pottery

indicators.note: put in means the girl's name goes inside the rearranged letters
original means inventive or novel, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: Jo March is a sister in Little Women

explanation.surface: A girl born in March claims the original pieces of a pottery set.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo March is the tomboy sister in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women, so 'March girl' is not a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Majolica is a kind of tin-glazed earthenware, originally Italian, so a type of pottery.

clue.text: Refurbish chapel a bit in established Order

indicators.note: refurbish means do up, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Redecorating part of a chapel for an established religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Established Order' suggests a church or monastic order; it is the order of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabetic means arranged in the sequence of the letters A to Z, a fixed and conventional ordering.

clue.text: A forward's hogging ball? That's concerning

indicators.note: hogging means keeping something to itself, so the forward's word wraps round the ball

parts.note: a prop is a rugby forward, so forward's gives PROP with S
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A rugby forward keeping the ball to himself is a worry.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the props are the forwards at either side of the front row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means with regard to, so as a preposition it means about or concerning.

clue.text: Emphatic type dismissed, caught

indicators.note: caught here means heard, as in catching what someone says

parts.note: a batsman is dismissed when bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer is out, caught, in heavy letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like another cricket dismissal, but it means overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold is the thick typeface used to emphasise words in print.

clue.text: Quiet commissionaire misses nothing, given time

indicators.note: misses means the zero is left out of the doorman

parts.note: a commissionaire is a uniformed doorman at a hotel or office
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A silent doorman misses out on nothing, given time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or temporarily at rest, as a sleeping volcano is quiet.

clue.text: Indian figurehead's three letters in a row

indicators.note: in a row says the three letters are consecutive in the alphabet, one after another

parts.note: the answer, split up, lists three letters of the alphabet joined by the word and

explanation.surface: An Indian leader's monogram of three consecutive letters.
explanation.walkthrough: List three letters in a row as G and H I: written out, the list spells the name. The setter leaves 'and' for the solver to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement and remains its symbolic national leader.

clue.text: Hurried to complete minutes in no particular order

parts.note: ran means hurried
to do a job is to complete it

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to finish the minutes of a meeting haphazardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means happening without pattern or method, without any set sequence.

clue.text: It strains fellow traveller visiting satellite perhaps

parts.note: co- means joint or fellow, as in co-pilot
a lander is a craft that travels to and sets down on a moon or planet

explanation.surface: Someone struggles as a communist sympathiser visits a moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow traveller' reads as a political sympathiser, but splits into fellow and traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl used in the kitchen to drain vegetables or pasta.

clue.text: Round some work up, nasty sort

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Round up some work for an unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, hence a cruel or frightening person.

clue.text: Poster impresses one Scottish golf club perhaps

indicators.note: impresses means presses in, so these letters are pushed inside the poster

parts.note: a placard is a poster or sign
yin is the Scots word for one
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An advert features a single Scottish golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club' looks like a unit, but golf gives G and club is the definition, an example of a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is one of the four suits in a pack of cards, so a card of that suit is an example.

clue.text: Look — one's taken in by a conjuror ultimately

indicators.note: taken in by means the one goes inside the following letters
ultimately means take the last letter of conjuror

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person is fooled by a magician's final trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests being fooled; here it places I inside A plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or appearance, as in an air of confidence, which is a look.

clue.text: Tips of plant, Chinese camellia?

indicators.note: tips are ends, so take the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Asking whether the leaf-tips of a Chinese camellia shrub are something.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea plant is Camellia sinensis, the Chinese camellia, and tea is made from its leaf tips.

clue.text: Appear expert on white horses?

indicators.note: on means the expert is placed after the white horses, riding on them

parts.note: white horses are foam-crested waves, surf
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Seem like an expert rider of waves.
explanation.walkthrough: White horses are breaking waves, not animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface means to come up into view or turn up, which is to appear.

clue.text: Significant space in medical speciality

parts.note: an em is a printer's space the width of an M
ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine

explanation.surface: A gap inside a branch of medicine that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means distinguished and important, so of notable significance.
